The Weierstrass Function

A function continuous everywhere yet differentiable nowhere. Add partial sums and the graph grows thornier.

Ordinary curves flatten when you zoom in. This one grows fresh teeth at every magnification. So no point ever earns a tangent line. Uniform convergence powers the continuity half.

For example, zoom into a 🌳 tree branch and smaller twigs appear, then smaller still, forever. At no magnification does the jaggedness smooth away.

The remaining terms cannot beat the spike: the terms with k<nk < nk<n are nearly flat at this scale (differentiating brings out akbkπa^k b^k \piakbkπ, a geometric sum with ratio ababab and a strictly smaller constant than the spike's), and the terms with k>nk > nk>n are uniformly tiny by the tail bound 2an+1/(1−a)2a^{n+1}/(1-a)2an+1/(1−a). Each partial sum WNW_NWN​ is a finite sum of cosines, hence smoothly (infinitely) differentiable on R\mathbb{R}R.

Yet WN→WW_N \to WWN​→W uniformly (problem 1) while WWW is differentiable nowhere (problem 2).

Conclude that a uniform limit of differentiable functions need not be differentiable.

Show proof

  1. Each WNW_NWN​ is a finite sum, so termwise differentiation is legitimate: WN′(x)=−∑n=0Nanbnπsin⁡(bnπx)W_N'(x) = -\sum_{n=0}^{N} a^n b^n \pi \sin(b^n \pi x)WN′​(x)=−∑n=0N​anbnπsin(bnπx) exists at every xxx.

    For instance W2′(x)=−πsin⁡(πx)−13π2sin⁡(13πx)−169π4sin⁡(169πx)W_2'(x) = -\pi\sin(\pi x) - \frac{13\pi}{2}\sin(13\pi x) - \frac{169\pi}{4}\sin(169\pi x)W2′​(x)=−πsin(πx)−213π​sin(13πx)−4169π​sin(169πx) (since a1b1π=13π2a^1 b^1 \pi = \frac{13\pi}{2}a1b1π=213π​ and a2b2π=169π4a^2 b^2 \pi = \frac{169\pi}{4}a2b2π=4169π​).

    Every curve on screen is a smooth function.

  2. But by problem 1's tail bound ∣W−WN∣≤(1/2)N→0|W - W_N| \le (1/2)^N \to 0∣W−WN​∣≤(1/2)N→0, we have WN→WW_N \to WWN​→W uniformly on R\mathbb{R}R. And by problem 2, the limit WWW is differentiable at no point.

  3. Hence a uniform limit of differentiable functions need not be differentiable — continuity is preserved under uniform limits (problem 1's argument), but differentiability is not. This is why analysis demands stronger convergence (e.g. uniform convergence of the derivatives) before differentiating termwise.
